cues.en: Mike: The law of large numbers.
cues.zh: Mike：大數法則。

cues.en: That sounds super grandiose, doesn't it, sounds very important and very fundamental.
cues.zh: 聽起來很宏偉，對吧？很重要、很根本。

cues.en: I imagine Moses was standing up on the mountaintop with three tablets, two tablets for the 10 commandments and one of 'em for the law of large numbers.
cues.zh: 我想像摩西站在山頂，拿著三塊石板，兩塊刻十誡，一塊刻大數法則。

cues.en: And it was just too difficult to carry all three at the same time, so he dropped the law of large numbers and it was lost to history for centuries, millennia.
cues.zh: 三塊一起拿太困難，所以把大數法則那塊掉了，失落了好幾個世紀、好幾千年。

cues.en: And then we rediscovered it.
cues.zh: 後來我們又重新發現它。

cues.en: And now in this video you are going to learn what the law of large numbers is and why it is so cool and so important for statistics and also just for scientific research in general.
cues.zh: 這部影片會學到大數法則是什麼，以及為什麼對統計和一般科學研究這麼酷、這麼重要。

cues.en: Okay, so let's dive right in.
cues.zh: 直接開始。

cues.en: Here is a definition of the law of large numbers.
cues.zh: 這裡是大數法則的定義。

cues.en: So as the number of experiment repetitions increases, so as we repeat the same experiment over and over and over again, the average of the sample means
cues.zh: 當實驗重複次數增加，也就是不斷重複相同實驗，樣本平均值的平均，

cues.en: better approximates the population mean.
cues.zh: 就會更好地逼近母體平均值。

cues.en: So we run the same experiment multiple times and then we start averaging our sample means.
cues.zh: 多次執行相同實驗，再開始把樣本平均值平均。

cues.en: So the results the mean of each individual sample, each experiment, we average those together.
cues.zh: 也就是把每個個別樣本、每次實驗的平均值，再一起平均。

cues.en: And the more we average together, the closer we get to the true population mean.
cues.zh: 平均得越多，就越接近真正母體平均值。

cues.en: That's also pretty cool because we typically don't know the true population mean.
cues.zh: 這很酷，因為通常不知道真正母體平均值。

cues.en: In fact, if we knew the true population mean we don't really need to do the experiment.
cues.zh: 如果知道，其實就不太需要做實驗。

cues.en: Okay, and here's what this law looks like written out in math terms, it might be some new symbols here, so let me walk you through this.
cues.zh: 這裡是用數學寫出來的法則，也許有新符號，我來說明。

cues.en: So this says the limit as n goes to infinity or as n approaches infinity.
cues.zh: 這表示 n 趨近無窮大時的極限。

cues.en: So basically this, the limit is what happens to this equation as n gets really, really, really large.
cues.zh: 基本上，極限就是當 n 變得非常非常大，這個方程式會如何。

cues.en: So n here is our number of experiment repetitions.
cues.zh: n 是實驗重複次數。

cues.en: This is not the sample size, it's not the same thing as the sample size.
cues.zh: 不是樣本大小，和樣本大小不是同一件事。

cues.en: It's the number of times that we are repeating the experiment over and over and over again, even though the sample size of each individual experiment is the same.
cues.zh: 是我們一再重複實驗的次數，即使每次個別實驗的樣本大小相同。

cues.en: Okay, so then we have here the average over n averages.
cues.zh: 接著，這裡對 n 個平均值取平均。

cues.en: So this is the, we take all the sample means from all the experiments that we've done so far and we average all of those averages together.
cues.zh: 取目前為止所有實驗的樣本平均值，再把它們全部平均。

cues.en: So the average of means minus mu, which is the true population mean, and you know, typically this is something we don't actually know.
cues.zh: 平均值的平均減去 μ，也就是真正母體平均值，這通常是我們不知道的。

cues.en: That's why we want to do the experiment and we want this quantity to better approximate this quantity.
cues.zh: 所以才想做實驗，希望這個量更好地逼近那個量。

cues.en: So we take their difference and we take the absolute value because we don't actually care if we are underestimating or overestimating the mean, we just make sure, we just want to get an estimate
cues.zh: 取兩者之差，再取絕對值，因為不在意低估還是高估，只想估計

cues.en: of how far off from the mean we are.
cues.zh: 和平均值究竟差多遠。

cues.en: So our error, you could think of this as an error, the difference between the sample means and the true population parameter.
cues.zh: 可以把這想成誤差，也就是樣本平均值和真正母體參數的差異。

cues.en: So greater than epsilon, this is a Greek little character epsilon.
cues.zh: 大於 epsilon，這是小寫希臘字母 ε。

cues.en: And epsilon is often used in calculus in particular in a proofs based calculus course to indicate some arbitrarily small number
cues.zh: epsilon 經常用在微積分，尤其以證明為主的課程，表示任意小的數，

cues.en: that is still greater than zero.
cues.zh: 但仍然大於 0。

cues.en: And that's actually the same concept as what computers do with epsilon.
cues.zh: 這其實和電腦使用 epsilon 的概念相同。

cues.en: So in MATLAB and in Python, there's a built-in variable or function called EPS for epsilon.
cues.zh: MATLAB 和 Python 有個叫 eps 的內建變數或函式，代表 epsilon。

cues.en: And that tells you what is the smallest number that your computer, your operating system, feels comfortable representing.
cues.zh: 告訴你，電腦、作業系統能夠放心表示的最小數字是多少。

cues.en: Okay, so all this says that the probability of not getting the right mean, so the probability of getting an error in our estimate, a divergence between the sample mean
cues.zh: 這整段就是說，沒有得到正確平均值，也就是估計出現誤差、樣本平均值

cues.en: and the population mean, the probability that that divergence is greater than zero is approaching zero.
cues.zh: 和母體平均值出現大於 0 的偏差，其機率會趨近於 0。

cues.en: So basically this gets better and better.
cues.zh: 基本上，結果會越來越好。

cues.en: Okay, so all of this compact equation just basically means this statement over here.
cues.zh: 所以這個精簡方程式，基本上就是這裡這句話。

cues.en: So why is the law of large numbers so cool?
cues.zh: 為什麼大數法則這麼酷？

cues.en: Well, it's so cool, it's so important because it means that any one sample or any one experiment can be driven by sampling variability,
cues.zh: 因為它非常重要，表示任何單一樣本或單次實驗，都可能受到抽樣變異、

cues.en: noise, all sorts of variation that I've discussed before and that you've seen in MATLAB code in several videos by now.
cues.zh: 雜訊，以及之前談過、在幾部 MATLAB 程式影片中看過的各種變異影響。

cues.en: So that also means that one sample or one experiment is unlikely to provide a good estimate of the true population mean.
cues.zh: 這也表示，單一樣本或單次實驗，不太可能很好地估計真正母體平均值。

cues.en: So we shouldn't put too much faith in any one individual experiment.
cues.zh: 所以不該太相信任何單一實驗。

cues.en: We shouldn't trust any one sample too much, but sampling from the same population many times or repeating the experiment multiple times,
cues.zh: 不該過度相信單一樣本，但從同個母體多次抽樣，或多次重複實驗，

cues.en: you might call this independent replications, can provide an accurate measure of the true population mean.
cues.zh: 也可以稱為獨立重複驗證，就能準確測量真正母體平均值。

cues.en: Even though we can't actually ever measure the true population mean, or you know, in many cases it's not feasible to measure the true population mean,
cues.zh: 即使實際上永遠無法測量真正母體平均值，或者很多情況下不可行，

cues.en: but sampling is pretty easy to do.
cues.zh: 但抽樣相當容易。

cues.en: So we can sample many times from the same population, average all those samples together, and we can be, the law of large numbers tells us that we can be pretty confident
cues.zh: 所以可以從同個母體抽樣多次，再平均所有樣本；大數法則告訴我們，可以相當有信心，

cues.en: that the average of multiple samples of the same population will quickly approach the true population mean.
cues.zh: 同個母體多個樣本的平均，會很快接近真正母體平均值。

cues.en: Okay, but here is an important question.
cues.zh: 但有個重要問題。

cues.en: How large is large that we don't, you know, that's not written into the law.
cues.zh: 多大才叫大？法則中沒有寫。

cues.en: The law doesn't say you need N of 17 experiments.
cues.zh: 沒有說需要 N=17 次實驗。

cues.en: So what does N need to be to get a reasonable estimate?
cues.zh: 那 N 要多少，才能得到合理估計？

cues.en: Well, unfortunately it's impossible to say because it depends on lots of experimental factors, it depends on the data, it depends on the measurement and so on.
cues.zh: 可惜無法直接回答，因為取決於很多實驗因素、資料、量測等等。

cues.en: So I can't just tell you exactly how many samples you need and how many repetitions you need to get a good estimate.
cues.zh: 我無法直接告訴你，需要多少樣本、重複多少次，才能得到好的估計。

cues.en: I will talk about this a little bit more in the section on statistical power and sample sizes, but the law of large numbers is basically something we think about operating at the scale
cues.zh: 統計檢定力與樣本數那一章會多談一點，但大數法則基本上是在

cues.en: of just repeating the experiment multiple times in more of a qualitative sense.
cues.zh: 定性意義上，透過多次重複實驗來理解。

cues.en: And it's a little bit difficult to put a quantitative number on it.
cues.zh: 很難直接指定一個定量數字。

cues.en: Okay, so here's an illustration, here's an example.
cues.zh: 這裡做個示範、看個例子。

cues.en: So we take a die, we roll it 50 times and we record the average of the numbers that we get after 50 rolls, and then we repeat this experiment 500 times.
cues.zh: 擲骰子 50 次，記錄這 50 次數字的平均值，再重複這個實驗 500 次。

cues.en: So this is our experiment, and then we repeat that experiment 500 times.
cues.zh: 這就是實驗，再重複 500 次。

cues.en: Now I actually did that on my computer and you'll get a chance to do that in the next video.
cues.zh: 我已經在電腦上做過，下一部影片也會讓你試。

cues.en: And my results look something like this.
cues.zh: 結果大概像這樣。

cues.en: So roll the die 50 times and record the average.
cues.zh: 擲骰子 50 次，記錄平均值。

cues.en: So compute the average, and you know, for experiment one, it turned out to be that the average was 3.85 or you know, whatever number that is.
cues.zh: 計算平均值，第一次實驗可能得到 3.85，或不管這個數字是多少。

cues.en: Here you see the results over all 500 experiments.
cues.zh: 這裡是全部 500 次實驗結果。

cues.en: And in orange is the expected value, we know that a fair die should have an average or an expected value of 3.5.
cues.zh: 橘色是期望值，我們知道公平骰子的平均或期望值應為 3.5。

cues.en: So it's interesting to note here that all of these individual averages are bouncing around the expected value.
cues.zh: 有趣的是，這些個別平均值都在期望值周圍波動。

cues.en: None of them, you know, they're not converging to the expected value.
cues.zh: 它們並沒有收斂到期望值。

cues.en: Sometimes we get really, really close and sometimes we're pretty far away.
cues.zh: 有時非常接近，有時差很遠。

cues.en: This one is pretty far away.
cues.zh: 這個就差很遠。

cues.en: Now this, the way that I'm showing the data here, this is not the law of large numbers.
cues.zh: 這裡展示資料的方式，並不是大數法則。

cues.en: What the law of large numbers tells us is that we have to start averaging each of these points together.
cues.zh: 大數法則告訴我們，必須開始將這些點一起平均。

cues.en: So rather than plotting the individual samples, we plot the cumulative average.
cues.zh: 因此，不畫個別樣本，而畫累積平均。

cues.en: So the first point here, well we've only done one experiment, so that's exactly the same, but already we get to the second point here and this is the average of the first two experiments.
cues.zh: 第一個點，因為只做一次實驗，所以完全相同；到了第二個點，已經是前兩次實驗的平均。

cues.en: And then the third point is the average of the first three experiments and so on, we get all the way down here.
cues.zh: 第三個點是前三次實驗的平均，依此類推，一直到這裡。

cues.en: And the 500th point here is the average of all 500 of these experiments, these repetitions.
cues.zh: 第 500 個點，就是全部 500 次實驗、500 次重複的平均。

cues.en: Now it's pretty interesting to see how quickly this converges to the expected value.
cues.zh: 很有趣，可以看到它很快收斂到期望值。

cues.en: By the time we get to here, 500 we're really spot on the expected value.
cues.zh: 到了 500 次這裡，幾乎完全命中期望值。

cues.en: But even here after only, you know, even 10 repetitions, we're already getting pretty close.
cues.zh: 但即使這裡，只重複 10 次，就已經相當接近。

cues.en: You know, still not exactly right with 10 repetitions, 10 averages of 10 experiments, 50 rolls each, but it's very, very close.
cues.zh: 10 次重複、10 次實驗的 10 個平均值，每次擲 50 次，還沒有完全正確，但非常接近。

cues.en: It's certainly closer than most of these points over here.
cues.zh: 肯定比這裡大多數點更接近。

cues.en: So that is the law of large numbers in effect, you'll get to see this yourself, you'll get to simulate these data in the next video.
cues.zh: 這就是大數法則發揮作用；下一部影片會讓你親自模擬資料，看到結果。

cues.en: And for now, I want to mention, the last thing I wanna mention is that it's interesting to look at the distribution of these numbers on the Y axis.
cues.zh: 最後想提，很值得觀察 Y 軸上這些數字的分布。

cues.en: So imagine taking each of these individual averages and projecting them down onto the Y axis.
cues.zh: 想像把每個個別平均值投影到 Y 軸。

cues.en: And what you might notice is that it seems like most of these numbers are clustered around the expected value.
cues.zh: 也許會注意到，大部分數字似乎集中在期望值附近。

cues.en: And as you get further and further away from the expected value, the numbers become sparser and sparser.
cues.zh: 離期望值越遠，數字越稀疏。

cues.en: So there's only one of these really extreme events.
cues.zh: 這麼極端的事件只有一個。

cues.en: And if you look down here, you know, there's fewer data points out at the extremes compared to as we get closer to the expected value.
cues.zh: 看下面也一樣，相較於接近期望值的位置，極端位置的資料點較少。

cues.en: So something interesting to contemplate for now, and I'll talk more about that in a later video.
cues.zh: 現在可以先想想，之後的影片還會討論。

cues.en: So in this video you learned about the law of large numbers.
cues.zh: 這部影片學到了大數法則。

cues.en: I explained what it is, and I showed you the formula that formalizes the law of large numbers.
cues.zh: 解釋了它是什麼，展示將它形式化的公式。

cues.en: And I showed you a demonstration of this phenomenon.
cues.zh: 也示範了這個現象。
